```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Ojara et al. (2023) analysed 365 patients with advanced non-small cell lung
cancer (NSCLC) from the CEPAC-TDM phase III study, who received paclitaxel
(3-h infusion) with carboplatin or cisplatin every 3 weeks for up to six
cycles. The paper contributes two models, packaged as two files:

* `Ojara_2023_paclitaxel_tgi` -- the tumor growth inhibition (TGI) model
  (Table 1): linear tumor growth and a first-order tumor decay driven by the
  per-cycle paclitaxel AUC (AUCcycle), whose strength declines exponentially
  with time. The file also carries the exponential time-to-event dropout model
  that the authors used for their visual predictive checks (Table S4,
  Appendix S1 equation 6).
* `Ojara_2023_paclitaxel_os` -- the Weibull time-to-event model of overall
  survival (OS) with baseline C-reactive protein (CRP) and the model-derived
  tumor size at week 8 relative to baseline (RS8) as covariates (Table 2,
  right column; NONMEM code in Appendix S1).

```{r model-info}
tgi <- readModelDb("Ojara_2023_paclitaxel_tgi")
os <- readModelDb("Ojara_2023_paclitaxel_os")
```

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(tgi)$reference`
* TGI model: `r rxode2::rxode(tgi)$description`
* OS model: `r rxode2::rxode(os)$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12937> (open access, PMC10681433)

# Population

The TGI model was estimated on all 365 patients (182 in the body surface area
(BSA)-guided arm receiving 200 mg/m^2 paclitaxel, 183 in the
pharmacokinetic (PK)-guided arm), with 1353 tumor size observations (RECIST
1.1 sum of target-lesion diameters) up to week 30. Because paclitaxel PK
samples were taken only in the PK-guided arm, the per-cycle paclitaxel AUC of
the BSA-guided arm was multiply imputed (50 replicates) from the paclitaxel
PK model of Henrich et al. (2017), and the TGI parameters for both arms
combined (Table 1) are the pooled multiple-imputation estimates. The median
baseline tumor size was 8.3 cm, and the median AUCcycle 18.4 umol*h/L (range
3.82-33.3) across cycles.

The OS model used the 221 patients with baseline measurements of all seven
blood biomarkers (CRP, interleukin-6, lactate dehydrogenase, carcinoembryonic
antigen, CYFRA 21-1, thyroid stimulating hormone and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte
ratio). Table S1 describes this subset: median age 64 years (41-78), 33.5%
female, 85.1% stage IV, 76.0% non-squamous adenocarcinoma, 82.8% carboplatin;
155 patients (70%) died during follow-up. The paper does not report race or
ethnicity.

```{r population}
str(tgi()$population)
str(os()$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `d/dt(tumor_size) = kgl - kkill * exp(-res * t) * AUC_PTX * tumor_size` | n/a | Equations 1-4 (Methods) |
| `tumor_size(0) = TUMSZ` (observed baseline) | n/a | Methods; IIV only on growth and drug-effect parameters |
| `lkgl` (Kg) | 1.03 um/h = 1.03e-3 mm/h | Table 1 |
| `lkkill` (beta02_pac) | 2.30e-5 (umol/L*h)^-1 h^-1 | Table 1 |
| `lres` (lambda) | 8.75e-4 1/h | Table 1 |
| `etalkgl`, `etalkkill`, `etalres` | CV 117%, 86.3%, 53.9% | Table 1 (variance = (CV/100)^2; see below) |
| `expSd` | 0.179 | Table 1, exponential residual model CV 17.9% |
| Dropout hazard `lam_haz * exp(beta * (BASE - TS)/BASE)` | n/a | Appendix S1, equation 6 |
| `llam_haz` (dropout lambda0) | 0.000473 1/h | Table S4, right column (both arms) |
| `e_tsshrink_haz` (dropout beta) | -1.88 | Table S4, right column |
| OS hazard `lambda * alpha * (lambda * t)^(alpha - 1) * exp(E_CRP*(CRP - 23.5)) * exp(E_RS8*(RS8 - 80))` | n/a | Equation 5; Appendix S1 `$DES` |
| `llam_haz` (OS lambda) | 0.00010 1/h | Table 2, Weibull covariate model |
| `lalfa_haz` (OS alpha) | 1.29 | Table 2, Weibull covariate model |
| `e_crp_haz` | 0.00744 per mg/L | Table 2, Weibull covariate model |
| `e_rcfb8_haz` | 0.0233 per % | Table 2, Weibull covariate model |
| Centring values CRP 23.5 mg/L, RS8 80.0% | n/a | Appendix S1 NONMEM `$PK` comments and `$DES` |

# Tumor growth inhibition model

## Closed-form checks of the drug effect

The drug effect per unit AUCcycle is `kkill * exp(-res * t)`. The paper states
that it falls by 58.6% by day 42 (end of cycle 2) and by 82.9% by day 84 (end
of cycle 4), and the Discussion converts the initial decay rate at the median
AUCcycle (18.3 umol*h/L) and median baseline (8.3 cm) into a shrinkage rate of
0.587 cm/week.

```{r closed-form-tgi}
ini_tgi <- tgi()$iniDf
th <- setNames(ini_tgi$est, ini_tgi$name)
kkill <- exp(th[["lkkill"]])
res <- exp(th[["lres"]])
kgl <- exp(th[["lkgl"]])

reduction <- 1 - exp(-res * c(42, 84) * 24)
shrink_cm_week <- kkill * 18.3 * 83 * 168 / 10

checks_tgi <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c(
    "Drug-effect reduction at day 42 (%)",
    "Drug-effect reduction at day 84 (%)",
    "Initial shrinkage rate (cm/week)"
  ),
  Model = c(100 * reduction, shrink_cm_week),
  Paper = c(58.6, 82.9, 0.587)
)
knitr::kable(checks_tgi, digits = 3)
stopifnot(abs(checks_tgi$Model / checks_tgi$Paper - 1) < 0.005)
```

## Typical tumor size profiles (Figure 3)

Figure 3 shows the tumor size at the median baseline (8.3 cm) and the median
AUCcycle given for six 21-day cycles, for three parameter combinations:
(a) the typical values, (b) a "worst case" with the 97.5th percentile of Kg
and the 2.5th percentile of beta02_pac, and (c) a "best case" with the 2.5th
percentile of Kg and the 97.5th percentile of beta02_pac (lambda at its
median in all three). Below, AUC_PTX is 18.4 umol*h/L during cycles 1-6
(weeks 0-18) and 0 afterwards.

```{r figure3-setup}
cycle_h <- 21 * 24
end_tx_h <- 6 * cycle_h
obs_h <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 30 * 168, by = 24), end_tx_h)))

profile_events <- function(id, auc = 18.4, base_mm = 83) {
  data.frame(
    id = id, time = obs_h, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "tumor_size",
    TUMSZ = base_mm,
    AUC_PTX = ifelse(obs_h < end_tx_h, auc, 0)
  )
}

z975 <- qnorm(0.975)
om <- function(eta) {
  sqrt(ini_tgi$est[ini_tgi$neta1 == ini_tgi$neta2 & ini_tgi$name == eta])
}
omega_sd <- c(kgl = om("etalkgl"), kkill = om("etalkkill"))
omega_sd_logcv <- sqrt(log(1 + omega_sd^2))

scenarios <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario, ~eta_kgl, ~eta_kkill,
  "(a) Typical", 0, 0,
  "(b) Worst case", z975 * omega_sd[["kgl"]], -z975 * omega_sd[["kkill"]],
  "(c) Best case", -z975 * omega_sd[["kgl"]], z975 * omega_sd[["kkill"]],
  "(c) Best case, omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)", -z975 * omega_sd_logcv[["kgl"]], z975 * omega_sd_logcv[["kkill"]]
) |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n()))

ev_fig3 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(scenarios$id, profile_events))
params_fig3 <- data.frame(
  id = scenarios$id,
  etalkgl = scenarios$eta_kgl,
  etalkkill = scenarios$eta_kkill,
  etalres = 0
)
# zeroRe() removes the random effects, so the eta columns of `params` set
# each scenario's parameter percentiles exactly. rxode2 warns that the
# multi-subject solve has no omega, which is the intent here.
sim_fig3 <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    rxode2::zeroRe(tgi), events = ev_fig3, params = params_fig3,
    covsInterpolation = "locf",
    returnType = "data.frame"
  ),
  warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  }
) |>
  left_join(scenarios[, c("id", "scenario")], by = "id")
```

```{r figure3-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(sim_fig3, aes(time / 168, tumor_size / 10, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = seq(0, 15, by = 3), linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey60") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 12)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Tumor size (cm)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Replicates Figure 3 of Ojara 2023 (median lines)",
    caption = "Dotted lines: paclitaxel doses (cycle starts)."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
```

Values read off Figure 3 of the paper are compared with the simulation below.

```{r figure3-table}
fig3_paper <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario, ~week, ~paper_cm,
  "(a) Typical", 6, 6.3,
  "(a) Typical", 12, 5.7,
  "(a) Typical", 18, 5.5,
  "(a) Typical", 30, 5.5,
  "(c) Best case", 6, 1.8,
  "(c) Best case", 18, 0.75,
  "(c) Best case", 30, 0.7
)
fig3_cmp <- fig3_paper |>
  left_join(
    sim_fig3 |>
      mutate(week = time / 168) |>
      select(scenario, week, model_cm = tumor_size) |>
      mutate(model_cm = model_cm / 10),
    by = c("scenario", "week")
  )
fig3_logcv <- sim_fig3 |>
  filter(scenario == "(c) Best case, omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)", time %in% (c(6, 18, 30) * 168)) |>
  pull(tumor_size) / 10
fig3_cmp$model_logcv_cm <- c(rep(NA, 4), fig3_logcv)
fig3_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Scenario = scenario, Week = week, "Figure 3 (cm)" = paper_cm,
    "Model (cm)" = model_cm, "Model, omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2) (cm)" = model_logcv_cm
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
typ <- fig3_cmp$scenario == "(a) Typical"
best <- fig3_cmp$scenario == "(c) Best case"
stopifnot(
  abs(fig3_cmp$model_cm[typ] / fig3_cmp$paper_cm[typ] - 1) < 0.1,
  # Values read off a figure: 15% admits the reading error, while the
  # alternative omega scale is 35-80% off at every time point.
  abs(fig3_cmp$model_cm[best] / fig3_cmp$paper_cm[best] - 1) < 0.15,
  all(fig3_cmp$model_logcv_cm[best] / fig3_cmp$paper_cm[best] > 1.3)
)
```

The typical profile (panel a) matches the figure within a few percent. This
also settles a units question: the Results text says a threshold AUCcycle of
4.49 umol*h/L is needed to start shrinkage, which equals `Kg / beta02_pac`
without the tumor size factor that Equation 2 requires. With the tumor size
included the threshold is `Kg / (beta02_pac * 83 mm)` =
`r signif(kgl / (kkill * 83), 3)` umol*h/L. A Kg 8.3-fold larger, which would
make the 4.49 statement exact, would have the typical tumor regrowing to
about 9 cm by week 30, which Figure 3a does not show. The Table 1 value is
used.

Panel (c) discriminates between the two usual readings of the CV% that Table
1 reports for the exponential IIV model. With `omega^2 = (CV/100)^2` the best
case plateaus near 0.75 cm, as in Figure 3c; with `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)` it
plateaus near 1.2 cm. The model uses `(CV/100)^2`. The worst-case panel (b),
which shows a nadir near 7.4 cm at week 8 before regrowth to about 9 cm,
is not reproduced by either reading (both give a monotonic increase): with
Kg at its 97.5th percentile it implies a decay rate only about 1.6-fold below
the typical value. The paper does not say how the percentiles of panel (b)
were obtained.

## Virtual cohort: week-8 tumor size and dropout

The paper does not report the distribution of AUCcycle beyond its median and
range. The cohort below draws one AUCcycle per subject from a log-normal
distribution with median 18.4 umol*h/L and log-scale SD 0.3, truncated to the
published range 3.82-33.3, and keeps it for all six cycles. Baseline tumor
size is log-normal with median 83 mm and log-scale SD 0.6, truncated to the
published range 10-383 mm (Table S1). These distributions are assumptions of
this vignette.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20231101)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20231101)
n_sub <- 200
cohort <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  auc = pmin(pmax(18.4 * exp(rnorm(n_sub, 0, 0.3)), 3.82), 33.3),
  base_mm = pmin(pmax(83 * exp(rnorm(n_sub, 0, 0.6)), 10), 383)
)
week8_h <- 8 * 168
obs_cohort <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 30 * 168, by = 168), end_tx_h, week8_h)))
ev_cohort <- cohort |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(time = obs_cohort) |>
  mutate(
    evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "tumor_size",
    TUMSZ = base_mm,
    AUC_PTX = ifelse(time < end_tx_h, auc, 0)
  ) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, TUMSZ, AUC_PTX)

sim_cohort <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  tgi, events = ev_cohort, covsInterpolation = "locf",
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
```

```{r cohort-vpc, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
sim_cohort |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim / TUMSZ, 0.05),
    p50 = quantile(sim / TUMSZ, 0.50),
    p95 = quantile(sim / TUMSZ, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 168)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 100 * p05, ymax = 100 * p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = 100 * p50)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Tumor size (% of baseline)",
    title = "Simulated tumor size relative to baseline (median, 5th-95th percentiles)",
    caption = "Compare with Figure 1 of Ojara 2023 (observed data, no dropout applied here)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The paper reports a median model-derived RS8 of 80% (a 20.0% reduction, range
-78% to +15%) across the individual (empirical Bayes) predictions. The
simulated week-8 values below use the individual model predictions without
residual error.

```{r rs8}
rs8 <- sim_cohort |>
  filter(time == week8_h) |>
  transmute(id, RCFB8_SLD = tumor_size / TUMSZ - 1)
rs8_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  Statistic = c("Median RS8 (%)", "5th percentile RS8 (%)", "95th percentile RS8 (%)"),
  Simulated = 100 * (1 + quantile(rs8$RCFB8_SLD, c(0.5, 0.05, 0.95), names = FALSE)),
  Paper = c(80.0, 42.4, 91.4)
)
knitr::kable(rs8_summary, digits = 1)
stopifnot(abs(rs8_summary$Simulated[1] - 80) < 12)
```

The paper's 5th and 95th RS8 percentiles (Table S5) come from the shrunken
individual estimates of the 221-patient subset, so the simulated spread,
which samples the full IIV, is wider.

The dropout model integrates the hazard `lambda0 * exp(-1.88 * shrinkage)`.
At no change in tumor size the hazard is 4.7 per 10,000 patients per hour and
at a 10% shrinkage 3.9, the "5 versus 4 in 10,000" quoted in Appendix S1. Of
the 365 patients, 84 (23%) still had tumor assessments after week 30
(Results).

```{r dropout}
haz <- exp(th[["llam_haz"]]) * exp(th[["e_tsshrink_haz"]] * c(0, 0.1)) * 1e4
knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(
    "Relative shrinkage" = c(0, 0.1),
    "Hazard per 10,000 patients per hour" = haz
  ),
  digits = 2
)
stopifnot(round(haz) == c(5, 4))

stay30 <- sim_cohort |>
  filter(time == 30 * 168) |>
  summarise(stay = mean(sur_drop)) |>
  pull(stay)
stay30
stopifnot(stay30 > 0.15, stay30 < 0.35)
```

The simulated probability of remaining in tumor follow-up at week 30 is
`r round(100 * stay30)`%, against 23% observed.

# Overall survival model

## Closed-form checks

With no interindividual variability, the Weibull survival function is
`S(t) = exp(-(lambda * t)^alpha * exp(E_CRP * (CRP - 23.5)) * exp(E_RS8 * (RS8 - 80)))`.
The paper quotes a median OS of 45 weeks at the median covariates, 103 weeks
when both covariates are at their 5th percentiles (CRP 1.18 mg/L, RS8 42.4%)
and 18.2 weeks when both are at their 95th percentiles (151 mg/L, 91.4%).

```{r os-closed-form}
ini_os <- os()$iniDf
tho <- setNames(ini_os$est, ini_os$name)
median_os_wk <- function(crp, rs8_pct) {
  m <- exp(tho[["e_crp_haz"]] * (crp - 23.5) + tho[["e_rcfb8_haz"]] * (rs8_pct - 80))
  (log(2) / m)^(1 / exp(tho[["lalfa_haz"]])) / exp(tho[["llam_haz"]]) / 168
}
os_checks <- tibble::tibble(
  Covariates = c("Medians (CRP 23.5, RS8 80%)", "Both 5th percentiles", "Both 95th percentiles"),
  CRP = c(23.5, 1.18, 151),
  RS8 = c(80, 42.4, 91.4),
  Paper = c(45, 103, 18.2)
) |>
  mutate(Model = median_os_wk(CRP, RS8))
os_checks |>
  dplyr::rename("CRP (mg/L)" = CRP, "RS8 (%)" = RS8, "Paper median OS (weeks)" = Paper, "Model median OS (weeks)" = Model) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
stopifnot(abs(os_checks$Model / os_checks$Paper - 1) < 0.05)
```

The same medians follow from solving the packaged model (the cumulative
hazard is integrated as an ODE, as in the NONMEM `$DES` block):

```{r os-solve}
ev_os <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  tibble::tibble(id = 1:3, CRP = os_checks$CRP, RCFB8_SLD = os_checks$RS8 / 100 - 1),
  time = seq(0, 200 * 168, by = 24)
) |>
  mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "cumhaz")
sim_os <- rxode2::rxSolve(os, events = ev_os, returnType = "data.frame")
solved_median <- sim_os |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(median_wk = approx(sur, time, 0.5)$y / 168, .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(solved_median, digits = 1)
stopifnot(abs(solved_median$median_wk / os_checks$Model - 1) < 0.01)
```

## Table S5 and Figure 5: one covariate at a time

Table S5 varies one covariate across its percentiles while the other follows
its distribution in the CEPAC-TDM data, and reports the median of the
simulated Kaplan-Meier curve. The individual data are not available, so the
other covariate is taken here as 200 equally spaced quantiles of a
distribution interpolated (on the log scale for CRP) through the published
percentiles: CRP 0.34 / 1.18 / 8.07 / 23.5 / 55.3 / 151 / 281 mg/L at the
0 / 5 / 25 / 50 / 75 / 95 / 100th percentiles (Tables S2 and S5) and RS8
22 / 42.4 / 64.8 / 80.0 / 86.0 / 91.4 / 115% (Results range and Table S5).
CRP and RS8 are treated as independent.

```{r tableS5}
qgrid <- (seq_len(200) - 0.5) / 200
p_known <- c(0, 0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95, 1)
crp_q <- exp(approx(p_known, log(c(0.34, 1.18, 8.07, 23.5, 55.3, 151, 281)), qgrid)$y)
rs8_q <- approx(p_known, c(22, 42.4, 64.8, 80.0, 86.0, 91.4, 115), qgrid)$y

tabS5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~covariate, ~level, ~paper_wk,
  "RS8", 42.4, 82.3,
  "RS8", 64.8, 57.4,
  "RS8", 86.0, 41.8,
  "RS8", 91.4, 34.0,
  "CRP", 1.18, 56.7,
  "CRP", 8.07, 51.0,
  "CRP", 55.3, 38.8,
  "CRP", 151.0, 24.0
) |>
  mutate(arm = seq_len(n()))

ev_s5 <- tabS5 |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(k = seq_along(qgrid)) |>
  mutate(
    id = (arm - 1) * length(qgrid) + k,
    CRP = ifelse(covariate == "CRP", level, crp_q[k]),
    RCFB8_SLD = ifelse(covariate == "RS8", level, rs8_q[k]) / 100 - 1
  ) |>
  select(id, arm, CRP, RCFB8_SLD) |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(time = seq(0, 200 * 168, by = 84)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "cumhaz")

sim_s5 <- rxode2::rxSolve(os, events = ev_s5, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame")
pop_surv <- sim_s5 |>
  group_by(arm, time) |>
  summarise(sur = mean(sur), .groups = "drop")
s5_cmp <- pop_surv |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(model_wk = approx(sur, time, 0.5)$y / 168, .groups = "drop") |>
  right_join(tabS5, by = "arm")
s5_cmp |>
  select(covariate, level, paper_wk, model_wk) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Covariate = covariate, "Level (CRP mg/L or RS8 %)" = level,
    "Table S5 median OS (weeks)" = paper_wk, "Model median OS (weeks)" = model_wk
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
stopifnot(
  abs(median(s5_cmp$model_wk / s5_cmp$paper_wk - 1)) < 0.1,
  max(abs(s5_cmp$model_wk / s5_cmp$paper_wk - 1)) < 0.2
)
```

```{r figure5, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
pop_surv |>
  left_join(tabS5, by = "arm") |>
  filter(level %in% c(42.4, 91.4, 1.18, 151)) |>
  mutate(
    panel = ifelse(covariate == "CRP", "(a) Baseline CRP", "(b) RS8"),
    percentile = ifelse(level %in% c(42.4, 1.18), "5th percentile", "95th percentile")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 168, sur, linetype = percentile)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 150)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Probability of survival", linetype = NULL,
    title = "Replicates Figure 5 of Ojara 2023 (median curves)"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Linking the two models

In the paper the OS model receives RS8 from the TGI model. The chunk below
feeds the week-8 tumor sizes of the simulated TGI cohort into the OS model,
pairing them with CRP values drawn from the interpolated CRP distribution.

```{r linked}
linked <- rs8 |>
  mutate(CRP = sample(crp_q, n(), replace = TRUE)) |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(time = seq(0, 200 * 168, by = 84)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "cumhaz")
sim_linked <- rxode2::rxSolve(os, events = linked, returnType = "data.frame")
linked_median <- sim_linked |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(sur = mean(sur), .groups = "drop") |>
  summarise(median_wk = approx(sur, time, 0.5)$y / 168) |>
  pull(median_wk)
linked_median
```

The population median OS of the linked simulation is
`r round(linked_median, 1)` weeks, against an observed median of 11.3 months
(about 49 weeks) in the abstract and a typical model value of 45 weeks.

# PKNCA

The packaged models take paclitaxel exposure as an input (AUCcycle) and have
no drug concentration output, so there is no concentration-time profile on
which to run a non-compartmental analysis. The checks above are on the
quantities the paper reports for these models.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **IIV scale.** Table 1 reports IIV as CV% without stating the formula. The
  variances are `(CV/100)^2`, the reading that reproduces the best-case
  profile of Figure 3c (see above). Under `log(1 + CV^2)` the variances would
  be 0.862, 0.557 and 0.254 instead of 1.369, 0.745 and 0.291. The residual
  error CV of 17.9% is used as the log-scale SD in the same way.
* **Kg units.** Kg is 1.03 um/h in Table 1 and is stored as 1.03e-3 mm/h. The
  Results statement that an AUCcycle of 4.49 umol*h/L is needed to start
  tumor shrinkage omits the tumor size from Equation 2; the Table 1 value is
  confirmed by Figure 3a and by the Discussion's 0.587 cm/week.
* **Paclitaxel exposure as an input.** The TGI model is driven by AUCcycle,
  which the authors derived from the paclitaxel PK model of Henrich et al.
  (2017, J Pharmacol Exp Ther 362:347-358). That PK model is not part of this
  package, so the user supplies AUC_PTX directly as a step covariate that is
  constant within each 21-day cycle and 0 after the last cycle ends. The
  paper defines AUCcycle per cycle but does not state the value after
  treatment ends; 0 is used, since no paclitaxel is given then.
* **Time origin.** The drug-effect decline `exp(-res * t)` uses the model
  time, so time 0 must be the first paclitaxel dose.
* **Platinum drugs.** Carboplatin and cisplatin were given at the same time
  as paclitaxel; their effect could not be separated and is absorbed into
  the paclitaxel drug effect, as in the paper.
* **Dropout model.** The dropout model of Table S4 (right column, both arms)
  is included in the TGI file because it depends on the predicted tumor size.
  Its reference BASE is taken as the observed baseline tumor size (TUMSZ).
* **RS8 covariate.** The paper's RS8 (percent of baseline) enters the OS
  model as `RCFB8_SLD`, the fractional change from baseline, with
  `RS8 = 100 * (1 + RCFB8_SLD)` computed inside `model()`; the coefficient and
  the centring value of 80.0% are unchanged.
* **Virtual cohorts.** The AUCcycle and baseline tumor size distributions of
  the TGI cohort, and the CRP and RS8 distributions used for Table S5, are
  interpolations of the published medians, percentiles and ranges, not the
  trial data. CRP and RS8 are treated as independent.
* **Sex percentage.** `population$sex_female_pct` of the TGI file is from the
  221-patient subset (Table S1); the paper does not tabulate demographics of
  all 365 patients.
